subject: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & benchmark methodology (EdgeFin)
messages:
From: Jordan Baker <jordan.baker@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@edgefin.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro & perf goals — post demo

Thanks for the demo today Marissa. Quick recap from our side:
- We need to validate P95 latency at 1k token prompt+streaming completion under 200ms (for single-token strides) at typical concurrency of 20 across 4 nodes.
- Target throughput is ~2,000 tokens/sec sustained for our main “trading_alerts” prompt set.
- Streaming quality: must support partial-token streaming (server pushes delta tokens) with <50ms per token delivery after first byte.

Could you share the prompt sets and the methodology you'd use to benchmark these? Also curious how you define warm vs cold start in your harness.

—Jordan
VP Engineering, EdgeFin
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Baker <jordan.baker@edgefin.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro & perf goals — post demo

Great notes Jordan — thanks. Below is a proposed plan and answers to your questions:

Plan / next steps
1) We’ll run an initial benchmark using your provided prompt set (you can send as CSV) and our public eval harness. Expected turnaround: 3 business days.
2) Baseline tests (no KV cache, cold start profile) + Steady-state tests (with KV/prefix caching enabled) to measure warm vs cold.
3) Concurrency sweep at 1, 5, 10, 20, 40 concurrent streams to map latency/throughput curves.
4) Streaming micro-bench: measure per-token latency (time from token ready to client receive) and backlog under load.

Measurement definitions
- P50/P95 token-latency: time between request start and token emission; for streaming we’ll report first-byte latency and per-token delta latency.
- Throughput: tokens/sec observed at service-edge aggregated across clients during sustained 60s windows.
- Cold start: instance scaled from zero, first request after idle > 10s.
- Warm start: instance with model fully loaded + cache primed via a 30s warmup run.

Deliverables
- Raw harness logs, reproducible benchmark script, prompt-set CSV, summarized PDF with plots.

Attachments: I’m attaching our benchmark guidelines and a sample prompt set template. Marcus will run the first pass and loop you back with results.

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-guidelines.pdf, prompt-template.csv

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Baker <jordan.baker@edgefin.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro & perf goals — post demo

Hi Jordan — quick technical notes from the bench run prep:
- For reproducibility we'll pin model version and quantization profile in the harness; can you confirm which model variant you want (gpt-redwood-13b-quant or gpt-redwood-70b-fp16)?
- Our harness supports the following metrics: per-token latency (ns resolution), aggregated token throughput, KV-cache hit rate, GPU utilization, p95 tail breakdown by step (decode/compute/transport).
- For streaming, we’ll instrument both server push latency and client-side assembly time. If you have a specific client (websocket vs SSE) let us know — we’ll emulate.

I’ll kick off a dry run today with a synthetic prompt set (to validate harness) and then swap in your CSV once you send.

Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Baker <jordan.baker@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@edgefin.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro & perf goals — post demo

Appreciate the clear plan — confirms scope. A couple quick answers:
- We’ll start with gpt-redwood-13b-quant.
- Client is websocket-based; partial-token stream is important.
- I uploaded the prompt set and a small test harness to the Drive link below (CSV + simple client). Please use those for the run.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/edgefin/benchmark-guidelines

Attachments uploaded: edgefin-benchmark-promptset-v2.csv, edgefin-eval-harness.zip

Looking forward to the results — thanks team.

—Jordan
